problems.field: assignment.what_was_assigned / assignment.structure: support for criterion 1 in the nested voice-gender comparison

form_value.nested_randomization_statement: When students selected voice, perceived female versus male AI voice was randomly assigned (pp. 3 and 10).
form_value.allocation_caveat: The paper does not fully specify the voice-gender allocation procedure across repeated users.

problems.source_says: The paper explicitly reports random assignment of perceived female versus male AI voice within spoken interactions. However, it does not explicitly establish randomized voice-gender order across repeated interactions by the same person, or describe a fixed participant-level voice assignment that would establish a between-person randomized comparison. The within-person order requirement therefore cannot be confirmed. This is missing support for the brief's unqualified randomized-assistance conclusion, not a contradiction of the form's accurately recorded randomization statement: the final form already acknowledges the allocation gap and codes criterion 1 as unclear. The observational voice-versus-text comparison cannot supply the missing randomization.
problems.quote: When the voice-based option was chosen, the perceived gender of CAiSEY’s voice (female versus male) was randomly assigned.
problems.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, first paragraph (voice-gender assignment) and second paragraph (repeated users and self-selected modality); p. 10, Supporting Information, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample and Modality Switching Across Successive CAiSEY Sessions. The complete Supporting Information, pp. 10-16, supplies no further voice-gender allocation/order procedure.

confirmed.statement: The final form codes S1 as observational and principal modality assignment as nonrandom; the PDF explicitly says users chose voice versus text for each interaction.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, second paragraph; p. 10, Supporting Information, Modality Switching Across Successive CAiSEY Sessions.

confirmed.statement: Perceived female versus male AI voice was explicitly randomly assigned after the user chose spoken interaction; these are nested configurations of CAiSEY.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, first paragraph; p. 10, Supporting Information, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample.

confirmed.statement: Participants developed their own business-case arguments while CAiSEY generated opposing arguments and responded in real time; the assigned voice concerned the AI they interacted with, not the identity of an output they merely evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 2-3, Approach; pp. 12-16, Representative Transcripts.

confirmed.statement: The paper frames the system as generative AI and describes sustained, responsive content generation; it names CAiSEY but supplies no underlying generative model or version.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 1-2, Abstract and Introduction; pp. 2-3, Approach; pp. 12-16, Representative Transcripts. Full-document review found no underlying model/version identification.

confirmed.statement: The voice and text conditions used the same case materials, prompts, and opposition strategy; the nested comparison was female versus male voice, and there was no human-only comparison arm.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, first paragraph; p. 6, Discussion, limitations paragraph.

confirmed.statement: Repeated observations do not establish randomized modality order: 186 of 203 users used both modalities, and the paper explicitly says its switching benchmark is not experimental randomization.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Approach, second paragraph; p. 10, Supporting Information, Modality Switching Across Successive CAiSEY Sessions.

confirmed.statement: The reported 458 voice and 499 text observations, including 218 male-voice and 240 female-voice observations, are conversations rather than randomized participant counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Supporting Information, Descriptive Statistics of the Study Sample.

confirmed.statement: All text measures were computed from user-only messages, and the nested voice-gender result is reported as a general statement of no evidence of persona effects.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 11, Supporting Information, Text Extraction; p. 5, Findings, final paragraph.

summary: The primary voice-versus-text comparison was self-selected, and the paper's nested voice-gender randomization does not explicitly establish randomized condition order across repeated users. The unqualified randomized-assistance conclusion is therefore unsupported under the requested check; the final form already acknowledges this gap and correctly leaves criterion 1 unclear.
